title: Gemista
subtitle: Greek baked tomatoes and peppers stuffed with herbed rice
excerpt: Ripe tomatoes and peppers hollowed out, filled with rice, olive oil, fresh herbs, and the scooped tomato pulp, then baked slowly until the vegetables are tender and the rice is cooked through. A summer dish that is served warm or at room temperature.
sourceNotes: Classic Greek home cooking, eaten across the country in summer when tomatoes are at their best.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Gemista is excellent at room temperature and keeps well in the fridge for 2 days. The flavour improves overnight.

content.text: Gemista means stuffed, and in Greece this almost always means tomatoes and peppers with rice. The trick is using the scooped tomato flesh in the filling so nothing is wasted. The rice is raw when it goes in and cooks fully inside the vegetables.

items.prepNote: cut into thick wedges, to fill gaps
for the base of the tin

content.text: Heat the oven to 180C. Slice the tops off the tomatoes and peppers and set the lids aside. Use a spoon to scoop out the tomato flesh and seeds into a bowl. Discard the seeds from the peppers.
Chop the tomato flesh roughly. Add the rice, onion, garlic, parsley, mint, olive oil, tomato puree, salt, and pepper. Stir well. The mixture will look very wet, which is correct.
Stand the hollowed tomatoes and peppers in the roasting tin. Fill each one three-quarters full with the rice mixture. Leave room for the rice to expand.
Replace the lids on each vegetable. Tuck the potato wedges into the gaps between the stuffed vegetables. Pour the water into the base of the tin.
Drizzle olive oil generously over everything. Cover the tin tightly with foil and bake for 60 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for a further 20 minutes until the tops are lightly browned and the rice is fully cooked. Rest for 15 minutes before serving warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The rice is still hard after baking.
items.cause: The filling was too dry or the foil seal let steam escape.
items.fix: Make sure there is plenty of liquid in the filling and the foil is sealed tightly. Add a splash more water to the tin and bake covered for another 15 minutes.

items.cause: They were baked too long or the oven ran hot.
items.fix: Check with a sharp knife after 50 minutes. Once the skin starts to wrinkle and soften, the vegetables are nearly done.

items.cause: Underseasoned or the herbs were added too early and lost their freshness.
items.fix: Season the filling generously before stuffing and taste a pinch of the raw mix before it goes in.
